data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves, approximately 6 to 7, are clearly seen radiating from the same node at the apex of the stem in all images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped tightly at the terminal end of the visible stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade attached to the stem, not divided into distinct leaflets)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): toothed (serrate) (distinct, regular, saw-like teeth are visible along the leaf margins)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are significantly longer than wide, with the widest point near the base and tapering toward the tip)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (the leaf tip tapers to a distinct, elongated point)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the base of the leaf blade tapers gradually to a wedge-like shape where it meets the petiole)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a single midrib is visible with secondary veins branching off from it)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): prominent and numerous (veins are clearly visible, running parallel to each other at a relatively consistent angle from the midrib to the margin)
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): dull (the leaf surface does not reflect light strongly, appearing matte)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): present (fine, short hairs are visible on the leaf surface, particularly noticeable on the younger leaves and along the veins in close-up views)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): short (the petioles are very short, causing the leaves to appear almost sessile and clustered at the stem tip)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the petioles appear round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (the stem appears firm and brownish, typical of a young tree seedling)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): present (fine hairs are visible on the stem, especially around the nodes where leaves attach)
    19.	Stem color: brown (the visible portion of the stem is a dark brown color)
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem surface appears relatively smooth without obvious ridges or large lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no clear stipules are visible at the leaf nodes)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling exhibits a distinct whorled leaf arrangement at its apex. The leaves are simple, lanceolate, and have serrate margins with prominent pinnate venation. Fine trichomes are present on both the leaves and the stem. A pink tag is attached to the seedling, likely for identification purposes.
